rows.evidence: Q1: Section 2 and Fig. 2 - the authors' lab has produced the annual irrigated-crop maps since 1998 and reports the mapped irrigated surface 1982-2016; Fig. 3 reports an own NDVI time-series case for a plot with several crop cycles. Q2: Section 2 - the authors report that under the 1998 agreement between the river basin authority and the users' board their maps have been used for water management, water rights assignments and sanctions; maps are shared by officials and farmers and sharing base information is described as crucial for solving conflicts; a Jury of Irrigation uses the SPIDER-ERMOT webGIS to provide evidence in sanction cases (Fig. 3); a May 2012 Supreme Court ruling set the conditions for satellite-based classification to count as evidence, referencing ERMOT. Q6: Sections 1-2 and Fig. 1 - the governance arrangement operates over the whole groundwater body (~10,000 km2, ~100,000 ha irrigated), i.e. irrigation scheme/aquifer scale. Q7: Section 2 - authors state that sharing the base information between officials and farmers is a crucial element for conflict solving, and the system rests on the formal agreement between the water authority and the users' board; Section 4 notes non-adapted rules and law as a barrier.
rows.notes: Largely an experience/lessons-learned account rather than a measured evaluation of governance outcomes; the 95% agreement figure on rights regularisation is attributed to ref [2], not the study's own data, and the usefulness of SPIDER-ERMOT for conflict resolution is asserted rather than quantified. No independent method, no mechanism measurement, single region, no dispersion. Stated limitations concern the water-accounting step (no comparative analysis of meters vs. crop-based allocation) and are framed as further research needs, not limitations of the governance result.

notes: Conference paper (WIT Transactions 2017) describing 20 years of remote-sensing-based irrigated-area mapping for groundwater governance in La Mancha Oriental, plus a proposed RS-based water accounting approach; text appears complete.
